architecture.mechanism: Chronic progressive dysfunction in specialized tissue layers caused by inflammatory accumulation, managed via structured diagnostic criteria and readiness assessment to ensure continuity of function during transitions.
architecture.intervention: Implement a multi-step diagnostic algorithm for the power steering system that assesses 'readiness' (fluid viscosity, seal integrity, electrical continuity) and 'disease control' (pressure consistency, leak rates) specifically under cold start conditions, treating the intermittent assist loss as a progressive degradation of the hydraulic-electromechanical interface.
architecture.expected_effect: Identification of the specific component failing the 'continuity' test during cold start, allowing targeted maintenance that restores consistent assist performance.
architecture.falsification_test: Perform a cold start pressure decay test on the power steering system after subjecting it to accelerated thermal shock cycles; if the intermittent assist loss persists despite passing all static 'readiness' checks (fluid level, wiring), the hypothesis that progressive tissue-like degradation (fluid breakdown or seal wear) is the cause is falsified.
